title: On Potentiality and Actuality Of Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.32991v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Foundation models are built through large-scale pretraining, often followed by post-training, and are then adapted to specific tasks and behaviors. But, does the adaptation add truly new capabilities, or the base model already holds it? We decompose the update induced by different adaptations into a component shared across all inputs and a residual that varies with the input. We find that the shared component suffices for most of the adaptation gain and can be learned directly: a shift adapter that learns a constant vector per layer, identical for every input, reproduces the behavior of LoRA and full fine-tuning. We call this the potentiality principle of foundation models: the base model already contains the capacity needed for task-specific expertise. To adapt to a new task, the model just needs to be actualized, i.e., pushed in a certain direction via a constant, input-independent shift. We show the implications of this principle on

translated_title: 论基础模型的潜能与实现
translated_abstract: 基础模型通过大规模预训练构建，通常随后进行后训练，然后再被适配到特定任务和行为上。但是，这种适配是否真正增加了新能力，还是基础模型本身早已具备这些能力？我们将不同适配方式所引起的更新分解为一个在所有输入间共享的分量和一个随输入变化的残差分量。我们发现，共享分量足以产生大部分适配增益，并且可以直接学习得到：一个在每层学习一个恒定向量（对所有输入均相同）的移位适配器，就能复现LoRA和全量微调的行为。我们将这一现象称为基础模型的潜能原则：基础模型本身已经包含了实现特定任务专业能力所需的容量。要适配一个新任务，模型只需被“实现”，即通过一个恒定的、与输入无关的移位被推向某个方向。我们展示了这一原则在……方面的意义。
tldr: 基础模型本身已蕴含完成特定任务所需的能力，适配并非添加新能力，而只需通过恒定的、与输入无关的向量移位将模型“实现”即可。
en_tdlr: Base models already contain the capacity needed for task-specific expertise, and adaptation merely actualizes this latent potential through a constant, input-independent shift rather than adding truly new capabilities.
